title: The foreach Loop
learning_outcomes: Explain what the foreach loop contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: iterating over arrays.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Control flow chooses which statements run and how many times. Every branch should cover the intended cases, and each loop should have a clear update and termination condition. In this lesson, focus on iterating over arrays; then compare it with keys and values. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use the foreach loop when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Control flow chooses which statements run and how many times. Every branch should cover the intended cases, and each loop should have a clear update and termination condition. For the foreach loop, begin with iterating over arrays. Also distinguish keys and values; associative array iteration; iteration by reference. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
